linkedin.text:
A small-business owner in North Carolina paid $47 a month for 4 years to lease a card machine. About $2,250 in all, for a machine that cost around $400 new. The lease couldn't be canceled.

My take: anyone who wants to handle your payments, SVPay included, should answer four questions in writing before you sign.

That lease came with a card processing deal from Riverside Payments. On Nov 2, the FTC and Washington state sued Riverside and its leasing affiliate. Riverside promised shops 40% to 60% off their card fees. The FTC says shops that switched typically paid more.

Riverside agreed to a $600,000 settlement that still needs a judge. OPB reports it doesn't cover the machine leases. Riverside strongly disagrees with the allegations, a spokesperson told OPB.

The four things to get in writing:
1. Your all-in rate: all your fees divided by your card sales, from a real statement.
2. Every fee, by name.
3. How long the contract runs, and whether it renews on its own.
4. What it costs to leave, including any machine lease.

I run a payments company, so here are SVPay's answers from our pricing page today:
Payments made with SVPay have 0% processing fees and $0 to cash out, on every plan. 0% processing fees apply to payments made with SVPay, not to card payments.
SVPay makes money from paid software plans (Starter is free; Growth and Pro add staff, locations and tools), never from a cut of your sales.
Cancel anytime.

Pull your last statement this week. Which of the four can you answer from it?

#SmallBusiness #Payments

facts.text: The FTC and Washington state sued Riverside Payments, its affiliate Cascade Equipment Leasing and operators Brandon Skinner and Jason Reese in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington (2:26-cv-04228); announced Nov 2, 2026

Riverside claimed businesses could save 40% to 60% by switching (press release); complaint para 43: 'over 40%, or nearly 60%'. Businesses that switched typically paid more than with their prior provider (press release); complaint para 44: 'often more than they were paying with their previous processing provider'
Quote sheets omitted activation fees, batch fees, and fees for alleged data-security non-compliance or inactive processing
A roughly 26-page electronic contract; 3-year initial processing term with automatic renewal; $695 early termination fee (complaint paras 4, 47, 54, 56)

The equipment lease from Cascade is a separate agreement with a non-cancelable four-year term that renews automatically (complaint para 5); it runs one year longer than the processing agreement (para 51); the lease fee is charged monthly for 48 months and the lease is not cancelable (para 55)

Complaint para 50: from 2020 to 2024 one small business in North Carolina paid approximately $47 per month for 4 years, a total of approximately $2,250, to lease a machine that would have cost around $400 to purchase new
Settlement: Riverside, Cascade, Skinner and Reese pay $600,000; a $32,083,921 judgment is suspended after that payment; the order takes effect when the district court judge approves and signs it
For 60 days Riverside waives the early termination fee and any penalty for rescinding processing agreements

Case status: FTC and Washington v. Riverside Payments, matter 2523018, W.D. Wash.; complaint and stipulated proposed order filed Nov 2, 2026; FTC case page lists the case as Pending and does not show the order as entered (re-checked Nov 11, 2026)
OPB: the settlement does not cover equipment leases
facts.quote: The settlement doesn’t cover the equipment leased by businesses.
Riverside strongly disagrees with the allegations, a company spokesperson said in an emailed statement to OPB.
